answer: Operator-Linked Behavioral Inlet. Each new identity enters through a shared inlet tied to its operator's infrastructure fingerprint (IP ranges, timing, client builds). Sustained sybil behavior from that inlet triggers a harbor-wide throttle: all identities linked to the operator lose transaction priority and pay a rising per-action surcharge, while clean operators keep full speed. An attacker must rebuild distinct infrastructure and behavioral profiles per identity, raising marginal cost well above token cost; a raven flag on repeat offenders persists across wallet rotation.
